title: Developer Experience: SDK Quickstarts, API Examples, Docs Site Ongoing Ops, and Top Support Issues
author: Maya Rodriguez
content:
Overview

This document consolidates developer experience (DevEx) guidance for SDK quickstarts, canonical API examples, docs-site operating procedures, and the top support issues with their canonical fixes. It is intended for documentation authors, SDK maintainers, developer advocates, and on-call engineers who handle developer support.

Goals
- Provide consistent, vetted SDK quickstarts and API examples for Python and Node.js.
- Reduce time-to-first-success for new developers.
- Standardize docs-site operating procedures (publishing, release tagging, hotfixes).
- Surface the top support issues we see in the field and provide canonical troubleshooting steps and fixes.

Audience
- Developer advocates and docs engineers (authors).
- SDK owners and maintainers.
- Support engineers and on-call.
- Product engineers shipping platform integrations.

Doc structure (what to update when)
1. Quickstarts & SDK guides: update when SDK release includes breaking changes or new feature flags.
2. API examples: update on model changes, feature launch (streaming, function calling), or deprecations.
3. Docs site ops: update when CI/CD changes, new linting rules, or new hosting infra is adopted.
4. Top support issues: update monthly with triage summaries from support rotation.

1) SDK Quickstarts (canonical)
Each quickstart follows the same pattern: goal, prerequisites, installation, minimal example, expected output, next steps. Keep examples < 30 LOC where possible.

Python quickstart (minimal text generation)
- Prerequisites: Python 3.10+, pip, Redwood API key (env REDWOOD_API_KEY).
- Install: pip install redwood-inference-sdk==1.4.2
- Example (short):
  from redwood import RedwoodClient
  import os
  client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.environ['REDWOOD_API_KEY'])
  resp = client.generate(model='redwood-2b', prompt='Translate to French: Welcome')
  print(resp.text)

Node.js quickstart (minimal chat)
- Prerequisites: Node 18+, npm, REDWOOD_API_KEY.
- Install: npm install @redwood/inference@^1.4.2
- Example (short):
  import Redwood from '@redwood/inference'
  const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY })
  const r = await client.chat.create({ model: 'redwood-chat-2b', messages: [{role:'user', content:'Summarize the benefits of caching.'}] })
  console.log(r.choices[0].message.content)

Recommended SDK configuration table
- Setting | Python | Node | Notes
- Recommended SDK version | 1.4.2 | 1.4.2 | Locked in quickstart; update when features added
- Default timeout | 30s | 30s | Override for long-running evals
- Streaming enabled | true | true | Default for chat streaming; opt out via stream:false
- Retry policy | idempotent: 3 | idempotent: 3 | Only retry idempotent calls by default

2) Canonical API examples
Include examples for the most-used surfaces: text generation, chat with streaming, embeddings, and function/tool calling. Each example must include: request payload, minimal response shape, and a note on cost/latency expectations.

Example: embeddings (Python)
- Use case: semantic search indexing.
- Snippet:
  vec = client.embeddings.create(model='sparse-embed-1', input=['document text here'])
  # vec.data[0].embedding -> list[float]

Example: function calling (Node)
- Show a simple tool call to a weather lookup. Demonstrate fallback when function not found.

3) Docs site operating procedures (owners: DevEx docs team)
Purpose: keep the docs site healthy and the quickstarts reliable.

Publishing workflow (CI)
1. Author edits markdown/Confluence source in Git (docs repo).
2. Create PR with preview build (Netlify/Vercel). PR must include: smoke test (basic page renders), code block syntax check, and linkcheck.
3. Reviewers: 1 technical reviewer + 1 content reviewer required.
4. Merge -> automatic staging deploy. Approve staging -> production deploy.

Release tagging and SDK-aligned docs
- Whenever SDK is published with breaking changes, create a docs patch: update quickstarts, add migration note, and tag release in repo `docs: vX.Y.Z`.
- Use a docs feature flag to render examples for multiple SDK versions where needed.

Hotfix process (broken examples or security-sensitive docs)
1. Create a hotfix branch off production.
2. Run smoke tests locally, push branch, and assign on-call docs owner.
3. If urgent, use expedited approval: 1 reviewer + lead; merge and deploy with rollback plan.

Operational checks (weekly)
- Linkcheck report: ensure no 404s on quickstarts.
- Code snippet execution: run a lightweight smoke harness that validates Python and Node snippets against a sandbox API key (non-production).
- Analytics: page view trends; if a quickstart page has >5% spike in support tickets, add a troubleshooting note.

4) Top support issues and canonical fixes (for DevEx + Support)
This section lists the most common issues, diagnostic steps, and canonical fixes. Keep language prescriptive and include CLI/SDK commands where helpful. Update with links to postmortems when applicable.

Issue A: SDK authentication failures (401 or missing API key)
- Symptoms: 401 responses, error message "invalid_api_key" or "missing API key".
- Quick diagnostics:
  1) Check env var: `echo $REDWOOD_API_KEY` (Linux/Mac) or `echo %REDWOOD_API_KEY%` (Windows).
  2) Confirm key format: starts with `rwd_` and length ~40 chars.
  3) Validate region restrictions: keys can be scoped; confirm key has permission for target environment.
- Canonical fix:
  - For env misconfiguration: update secrets manager or CI variable and redeploy.
  - For expired/rotated keys: rotate in console -> update running service and retry.
  - For permission issues: escalate to platform-security to inspect key scope.

Issue B: Streaming disconnects or truncated responses
- Symptoms: partial stream, socket closed errors, "aborted by client" logs.
- Quick diagnostics:
  1) Check client-side network/timeouts. Increase read timeout to 60s and retry.
  2) Inspect proxy/load balancer (ALB/Nginx/Envoy) for idle timeout < server stream duration.
  3) Review SDK version: older SDKs had a reconnect regression (see changelog).
- Canonical fix:
  - Update SDK to latest patch that fixes streaming reconnects.
  - Increase LB/webserver idle_timeout to 120s.
  - If using serverless (Lambda), use direct-invoke pattern or a buffering proxy to avoid cold-start drops.

Issue C: Large embedding requests OOM or timeout
- Symptoms: worker OOMs, timeouts for batches > 512 inputs, or 413 payload errors.
- Quick diagnostics:
  1) Check request size, tokens per input, and batch size.
  2) Inspect runtime logs for OOM stack traces.
- Canonical fix:
  - Enforce client-side batching: limit batches to 128 inputs or 32k tokens total.
  - Use the async/bulk embeddings endpoint (if available) for very large jobs.
  - Recommend quantized model variants for memory-sensitive workloads.

Issue D: Unexpected model output regression after deployment
- Symptoms: increase in customer complaints, eval score drop on known prompt set.
- Quick diagnostics:
  1) Check model version rollback history and rollout policy (canary vs full).
  2) Run the failing prompt set through the eval harness (link to applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness).
- Canonical fix:
  - Roll back to previous model variant, open regression ticket against model-onboarding.
  - Re-run quality checks and add new test cases to the regression suite.

Issue E: Docs examples fail due to SDK minor version mismatch
- Symptoms: Syntax errors or missing parameter names in code snippets.
- Quick diagnostics:
  1) Verify SDK version in snippet header and installed version.
  2) Check changelog for breaking renames.
- Canonical fix:
  - Maintain versioned examples (v1.x, v2.x). Add a short note at top of page: "This example requires @redwood/inference >=1.4.0".
  - Update snippet CI to execute representative snippets against latest stable SDK.

Appendices
A. Snippet testing harness (authoring checklist)
- Every new quickstart must pass: linkcheck, code-lint, snippet-exec (Py/Node), and a reviewer sign-off.
- Tests run in CI using a sandbox API key with rate limits.

B. Ownership and escalation
- Docs owner: DevEx docs team (on-call rotation: maya@redwood.com -> next: ethan@redwood.com).
- SDK owner: platform-sdk team.
- For incidents impacting >5% of customers: page on-call SRE and product manager.

C. Change log (recent significant updates)
- 2026-05-10: initial combined guideline and quickstarts consolidation.
- 2026-08-14: added streaming troubleshooting steps and snippet execution CI.
- 2026-11-02: expanded canonical fixes for embeddings OOM and added hotfix process.
